image:image.image:title: Only 2 of 39,676 public AI-search research queries ask AI to find a local provider
image:image.image:caption: Across four public AI-search datasets, 239 of 39,676 unique queries (0.6%) concern a physical business, and only 2 ask an AI to find a local service provider.

image:image.image:title: Local business searches trigger Google AI Overviews more than any other topic
image:image.image:caption: 76.4% of local-business searches showed a Google AI Overview, nearly double the next category (science, 39.9%) and over five times the 13.7% average.

image:image.image:title: Local searches got an AI answer 76% of the time, even more often than other questions
image:image.image:caption: Controlling for phrasing, local searches were still 12 points more likely to get an AI Overview than other question-style searches (76.4% vs 64.1%).

image:image.image:title: Who Google’s AI cites for local business questions vs everything else
image:image.image:caption: In local answers, Gannett newspapers supplied 28.3% of citations and appeared in 90.3% of answers. Businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5% of citations.

image:image.image:title: TEGNA TV stations are 18 times more likely to be cited in local answers than in other answers
image:image.image:caption: Relative to other topics, local answers lean on TEGNA TV stations 18 times more, AOL/Yahoo/MSN 4.1 times and Gannett 3.9 times. Social media is used less (0.7 times).

image:image.image:title: The 18 websites Google’s AI cited most for “is it open” questions
image:image.image:caption: today.com was cited in 62% of local answers and usatoday.com in 47%. Gannett and TEGNA domains are highlighted; no store’s own site made the top 18.

image:image.image:title: Local gatekeepers: which sources dominate Google AI’s local answers
image:image.image:caption: Gannett newspapers and other news outlets are local gatekeepers: large shares of local citations and over-represented versus other topics. Business sites sit near the bottom left.

image:image.image:title: The vaguer the local question, the less the business gets cited
image:image.image:caption: Businesses’ own sites made up 8.8 to 10.9% of citations when a brand was named, but only 1.0% for generic “what’s open” questions, which is how people discover new places.

image:image.image:title: Brand by brand: where Google’s AI got each chain’s hours
image:image.image:caption: Walmart, the most-asked brand, had its own site cited in 7% of its answers. Starbucks and Chipotle were never cited for their own hours; Publix, Trader Joe’s and Sam’s Club were cited every time.

image:image.image:title: Ranked on page one, skipped by the AI: brand websites in local answers
image:image.image:caption: Brand websites appeared on page one in 147 of 157 brand questions but were cited in 70. Walmart ranked in 11 of 15 answers and was cited once.

image:image.image:title: Ranked and used vs ranked and ignored: a 2x2 of brand websites
image:image.image:caption: Most brands ranked on page one nearly every time. What split them was use: Publix, Trader Joe’s and Sam’s Club were cited every time; Walmart, Starbucks and Chipotle were ranked but ignored.

image:image.image:title: The AI goes past page one for news, not for business websites
image:image.image:caption: Only 4.1% of business-site citations came from outside Google’s first page, versus 48.8% for AOL/Yahoo/MSN and 39.8% for TEGNA stations. A business site has to rank to be used.

image:image.image:title: 173 of 207 local AI answers told people to check with their local store
image:image.image:caption: 83.6% of local AI answers sent the reader back to the store (“check your local store,” “call ahead,” “hours may vary”), against 2.6% of other answers.

image:image.image:title: 1 of 207 local AI answers named a street address or phone number
image:image.image:caption: Only 1 of 207 local AI answers gave a street address or phone number. The AI answered about chains, not places.

image:image.image:title: AI answers local questions with national facts
image:image.image:caption: 65.7% of local answers spoke about “all locations” or “most stores” (vs 2.3% of other answers), and 83.6% hedged (vs 2.6%). National facts are the AI’s default for local questions.

image:image.image:title: When Google’s AI says “the store locator says,” half the time it can’t show it
image:image.image:caption: 16 of 31 local claims that cited a store locator, app or official site (51.6%) were not supported by any page the AI cited, against 6.7% of other local claims.

image:image.image:title: Local AI answers were more faithful to their sources than average
image:image.image:caption: 87.8% of 2,253 local claims were supported by the cited pages, versus 84.5% of 95,767 other claims. Faithful to sources is not the same as accurate for your location.

image:image.image:title: Cited vs readable: what Google’s AI could actually read
image:image.image:caption: News pages were both cited and readable. Social posts were cited in 48% of local answers but 78% were thin (median 8 words). 11% of businesses’ own pages were thin.

image:image.image:title: Social posts the AI cited had a median of 8 readable words
image:image.image:caption: The median cited social post had 8 readable words. Store locator pages were also thin: Trader Joe’s store search had 97 words and Cracker Barrel’s Easter page 18.

image:image.image:title: Ask the same thing in different words and two-thirds of the sources change
image:image.image:caption: “Is Target open on Easter” and “Target Easter hours,” asked the same day, shared about 35% of cited sources on average. The verdict stayed the same; the sources rotated.

image:image.image:title: Local AI answers cite fewer sources: 7.2 per answer vs 8.1
image:image.image:caption: Local AI Overviews cited 7.23 sources on average versus 8.1 for other topics, clustered at 5 to 8 sources.

image:image.image:title: Local “is it open” searches spiked the day after Easter
image:image.image:caption: 185 of 271 local searches in the dataset were collected on April 6, 2026, the day after Easter, which is why most local answers in this study are about holiday hours.

image:image.image:title: Local AEO priority map: what AI cites vs what you control
image:image.image:caption: The sources AI cites most for local answers (news) are the ones businesses control least, and the source they fully control (their site) is cited least. AEO closes that gap from both sides.

image:image.image:title: SEO gets you into the list. AEO gets you into the answer.
image:image.image:caption: Search engine optimization (SEO) earns a place in a list of links. Answer engine optimization (AEO) earns a place inside the AI-written answer that appears before any links.

image:image.image:title: How Google’s AI builds an answer about a local business
image:image.image:caption: For local questions, Google’s AI assembled answers mostly from news coverage (67.5% of citations), rarely from the business itself (6.5%), and usually ended by telling people to check with their local store.

image:image.image:title: Ranked first, still skipped: why SEO alone isn’t AEO
image:image.image:caption: In 147 of 157 brand questions the store’s own site ranked on page one, but the AI cited it in only 70. Ranking and being used by AI are separate outcomes.

image:image.image:title: What Google’s AI can actually read on a page
image:image.image:caption: News pages the AI cited had about 500 readable words. Store locator pages were mostly scripts, and the median cited social post had 8 readable words.

image:image.image:title: One confirmed record, pushed everywhere AI looks
image:image.image:caption: Because AI rotates between sources, a business’s facts need to match on its website, Google Business Profile, directories and press. Local AI Registry starts from one owner-confirmed record.

image:image.image:title: Different wording, different sources, same answer
image:image.image:caption: Three ways of asking about Target on Easter returned the same verdict but shared only about a third of their sources. No single publisher owns a local answer.
